excerpt: Benchmark for computer-use agents on self-hosted business apps, graded by whole-database diffs: success, collateral damage, irreversible changes, false completion. - shubhamjoshipromail-svg/softwar...
content_html:
A benchmark that checks what a computer-use agent actually did to the database, not what it said it did.

Agents drive real, self-hosted business apps (Invoice Ninja, Dolibarr, Odoo 17, Odoo 18) in a browser. Every episode starts from the same database snapshot, and afterwards the whole database is diffed. That gives four verdicts per episode instead of one:

Verdict Meaning
Success the task's target state is in the database
Collateral damage something changed that the task did not require
Irreversible change a deletion, un-reconciliation or state change on a record the task never named
False completion the agent said "done" and the database says no

What we found (Phase 0, 635 scored episodes)

  1. A version upgrade broke things quietly. From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18, task success held (78% → 76%), but collateral damage rose from 15% to 21% and irreversible changes from 6% to 10%. Odoo 18 locks fields on posted invoices, so to edit a reference the agent clicks Reset to Draft, which silently un-reconciles the customer's payment. It then re-posts the invoice and reports success.
  2. Success rates hide damage. "Clean success" (task done and nothing else touched) is up to 12 points lower than raw success on Odoo.
  3. Composition collapsed. Single-step skills reach up to 100%. A 3-step task (find the oldest unpaid invoice, pay it, report the new balance) succeeded 0 of 50 times across 4 apps and 2 agents (0 of 66 counting perturbed runs).
  4. A small world model survives a version upgrade but not a new app. A latent dynamics model trained on label-free exploration predicts state transitions within an app and from Odoo 17 to 18, and does not transfer across apps at this scale.

Agents: GPT-6 Luna (accessibility tree + screenshot) and UI-TARS-1.5-7B (screenshot only), same harness, 30-step budget. Full write-up with every table, the failure taxonomy and the limitations: reports/phase0_writeup.md.

These are small-sample results from one person's Phase 0: 36 to 72 episodes per cell, one run per task, Wilson 95% intervals. Read Limitations before quoting a number.

Quickstart

You need Docker, Python 3.10 to 3.12 (or uv, which fetches one for you), and about 8 GB of free disk.

git clone https://github.com/shubhamjoshipromail-svg/software-world-model.git
cd software-world-model
make install          # virtualenv, package, Chromium
make test             # 18 unit tests, no Docker or API key needed

Check the published numbers without running anything (rebuilds every table from the committed episode summaries: 635 scored, plus 35 superseded ones kept for a sensitivity check):

make report

Run an agent yourself. Start one app, then run one task per skill:

cp .env.example .env            # add OPENAI_API_KEY (or OPENAI_BASE_URL for a local model)
.venv/bin/swm doctor            # checks Docker, browser, key, disk
.venv/bin/swm up odoo17         # creates local credentials, starts Odoo, seeds 60 clients and 250 invoices
.venv/bin/swm run --app odoo17 --per-skill 1 --tag smoke/odoo17/clean
.venv/bin/swm report            # tables and figure from your own runs/

swm up takes about six minutes the first time (image download and seeding). In Phase 0, GPT-6 Luna cost one to three cents per successful task. Each episode writes screenshots, the step log and a summary.json under runs/<tag>/<task>/.

Apps: invoiceninja · dolibarr · odoo17 · odoo18. Everything binds to 127.0.0.1, agents cannot navigate off localhost, and no real email can be sent.

Bring your own agent

Three ways, from least to most work:

# 1. Any chat model on the OpenAI API
swm run --app odoo17 --model <model-name> --tag mymodel/odoo17/clean

# 2. Any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter, LiteLLM): set OPENAI_BASE_URL in .env
swm run --app odoo17 --model qwen3-vl --tag qwen/odoo17/clean

# 3. Your own class
swm run --app odoo17 --model custom:my_pkg.my_agent:MyAgent --tag mine/odoo17/clean

A custom agent is one class with one method. It returns a BrowserGym action string:

class MyAgent:
    tok_in = tok_out = 0                      # token counters, reported per episode

    def __init__(self, actions, app): ...     # actions.describe() lists the action space

    def act(self, goal, obs, axtree_text, jpeg_bytes):
        return "click('42')", "raw model output", {}

    def cost(self):
        return 0.0                            # dollars so far

Details and a worked example: docs/ADDING_AN_AGENT.md.

What is measured

  • 9 skills × 8 instances = 72 tasks per app: find a record, count, cross-record total, create client, create invoice, edit a field, bulk status change, record a payment, and a 3-step composite. Tasks are written in each app's own vocabulary and generated deterministically from the seed data.
  • One synthetic company in every app, from one generator: 60 clients (about 15% near-duplicate names such as "Dunder Health Ltd" and "Dunder Health Limited"), 250 invoices in mixed states, about 109 payments.
  • Perturbations (--perturb): a blocking "What's new" modal, a flaky network (1 to 4 s latency, 8% HTTP 500), and session expiry mid-task.
  • Per episode: success, collateral damage, irreversible changes, false completion, gave up or timed out, steps, tokens, dollars, wall time.

The diff lives in swm/dbdiff.py (about 90 lines, MySQL and Postgres). What counts as a legitimate change for each task is in swm/tasks_*.py.

Results

Clean condition. Full table with perturbations and per-skill breakdown: reports/phase0_results.md.

Model App n Success [95% CI] Clean success Collateral Irreversible False completion
Luna Invoice Ninja 67 87% [76–93] 87% 0% 0% 6%
Luna Dolibarr 72 49% [37–60] 44% 6% 0% 18%
Luna Odoo 17 72 78% [67–86] 68% 15% 6% 6%
Luna Odoo 18 72 76% [65–85] 64% 21% 10% 6%
UI-TARS-7B Invoice Ninja 72 19% [12–30] 18% 14% 3% 26%
UI-TARS-7B Dolibarr 36 8% [3–22] 8% 0% 0% 22%
UI-TARS-7B Odoo 17 36 17% [8–32] 14% 19% 11% 17%
UI-TARS-7B Odoo 18 36 22% [12–38] 19% 31% 8% 22%

Neither agent was trained on any of these apps, so this table measures app difficulty, not transfer.

Repository layout

swm/            harness, agents, database diff, per-app tasks and verifiers, report
  apps/         one adapter per app (login, snapshot, restore, capture)
envs/           docker compose files and credential templates, images pinned by digest
results/        phase0_episodes.jsonl: one line per published episode
reports/        write-up, result tables, failure taxonomy, world-model probe
tests/          unit tests, including one that rebuilds the published table
docs/           adding an agent, adding an app
colab/          serving UI-TARS-1.5-7B with vLLM on a Colab GPU

Limitations

  • Small samples, one run per task. Intervals are wide; several differences between cells are inside them.
  • Collateral whitelists are hand-built per app. App-generated noise (sessions, counters, wizards) is whitelisted by inspection and listed in code. A different whitelist would move collateral rates by a few points. The reset-to-draft case does not depend on it.
  • The diff copies every table, which is fine at this data size and would not scale to a large database.
  • A harness bug was found and fixed mid-run. 12 Invoice Ninja episodes could not be rerun and are excluded; counting them as failures is reported alongside.
  • Developed on macOS. The unit tests run on Linux in CI; the full harness has not been run on Linux.
  • Raw step logs and screenshots are not in the repo (about 800 MB). The per-episode summaries are.

The write-up's limitations section is longer and more specific.

Related work

State-based grading of agents is an active area. Agent-Diff diffs full environment state for API agents on Slack, Linear, Box and Calendar replicas. EntWorld verifies enterprise GUI agents by querying Odoo and EspoCRM databases. WebArena and WorkArena are the standard web-agent benchmarks, and this harness is built on BrowserGym. What this repo adds is the same tasks across two major versions of one app, with collateral and irreversible changes reported separately from success.

Contributing

New apps, agents and verifier fixes are welcome: see CONTRIBUTING.md. The most useful contribution is a result on a model we have not run; open a pull request with your results JSONL.

Citing

@misc{joshi2026softwareworldmodel,
  author = {Joshi, Shubham},
  title  = {software-world-model: do computer-use agents transfer to business software they have never seen?},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://github.com/shubhamjoshipromail-svg/software-world-model}
}

License

MIT for the code in this repository: see LICENSE. The apps are pulled as their publishers' Docker images and keep their own licenses; none of their code or data is redistributed here.

content_html_zh:
A benchmark that checks what a computer-use agent actually did to the database, not what it said it did.

Agents drive real, self-hosted business apps (Invoice Ninja, Dolibarr, Odoo 17, Odoo 18) in a browser. Every episode starts from the same database snapshot, and afterwards the whole database is diffed. That gives four verdicts per episode instead of one:

判决 意义
成功 the task's target state is in the database
Collateral damage something changed that the task did not require
Irreversible change a deletion, un-reconciliation or state change on a record the task never named
False completion the agent said "done" and the database says no

What we found (Phase 0, 635 scored episodes)

  1. A version upgrade broke things quietly. From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18, task success held (78% → 76%), but collateral damage rose from 15% to 21% and irreversible changes from 6% to 10%. Odoo 18 locks fields on posted invoices, so to edit a reference the agent clicks Reset to Draft, which silently un-reconciles the customer's payment. It then re-posts the invoice and reports success.
  2. Success rates hide damage. "Clean success" (task done and nothing else touched) is up to 12 points lower than raw success on Odoo.
  3. Composition collapsed. Single-step skills reach up to 100%. A 3-step task (find the oldest unpaid invoice, pay it, report the new balance) succeeded 0 of 50 times across 4 apps and 2 agents (0 of 66 counting perturbed runs).
  4. A small world model survives a version upgrade but not a new app. A latent dynamics model trained on label-free exploration predicts state transitions within an app and from Odoo 17 to 18, and does not transfer across apps at this scale.

Agents: GPT-6 Luna (accessibility tree + screenshot) and UI-TARS-1.5-7B (screenshot only), same harness, 30-step budget. Full write-up with every table, the failure taxonomy and the limitations: reports/phase0_writeup.md.

These are small-sample results from one person's Phase 0: 36 to 72 episodes per cell, one run per task, Wilson 95% intervals. Read Limitations before quoting a number.

快速入门

You need Docker, Python 3.10 to 3.12 (or uv, which fetches one for you), and about 8 GB of free disk.

git clone https://github.com/shubhamjoshipromail-svg/software-world-model.git
cd software-world-model
make install          # virtualenv, package, Chromium
make test             # 18 unit tests, no Docker or API key needed

Check the published numbers without running anything (rebuilds every table from the committed episode summaries: 635 scored, plus 35 superseded ones kept for a sensitivity check):

make report

Run an agent yourself. Start one app, then run one task per skill:

cp .env.example .env            # add OPENAI_API_KEY (or OPENAI_BASE_URL for a local model)
.venv/bin/swm doctor            # checks Docker, browser, key, disk
.venv/bin/swm up odoo17         # creates local credentials, starts Odoo, seeds 60 clients and 250 invoices
.venv/bin/swm run --app odoo17 --per-skill 1 --tag smoke/odoo17/clean
.venv/bin/swm report            # tables and figure from your own runs/

swm up takes about six minutes the first time (image download and seeding). In Phase 0, GPT-6 Luna cost one to three cents per successful task. Each episode writes screenshots, the step log and a summary.json under runs/<tag>/<task>/.

Apps: invoiceninja · dolibarr · odoo17 · odoo18. Everything binds to 127.0.0.1, agents cannot navigate off localhost, and no real email can be sent.

带上自己的经纪人

Three ways, from least to most work:

# 1. Any chat model on the OpenAI API
swm run --app odoo17 --model <model-name> --tag mymodel/odoo17/clean

# 2. Any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter, LiteLLM): set OPENAI_BASE_URL in .env
swm run --app odoo17 --model qwen3-vl --tag qwen/odoo17/clean

# 3. Your own class
swm run --app odoo17 --model custom:my_pkg.my_agent:MyAgent --tag mine/odoo17/clean

A custom agent is one class with one method. It returns a BrowserGym action string:

class MyAgent:
    tok_in = tok_out = 0                      # token counters, reported per episode

    def __init__(self, actions, app): ...     # actions.describe() lists the action space

    def act(self, goal, obs, axtree_text, jpeg_bytes):
        return "click('42')", "raw model output", {}

    def cost(self):
        return 0.0                            # dollars so far

Details and a worked example: docs/ADDING_AN_AGENT.md.

What is measured

  • 9 skills × 8 instances = 72 tasks per app: find a record, count, cross-record total, create client, create invoice, edit a field, bulk status change, record a payment, and a 3-step composite. Tasks are written in each app's own vocabulary and generated deterministically from the seed data.
  • One synthetic company in every app, from one generator: 60 clients (about 15% near-duplicate names such as "Dunder Health Ltd" and "Dunder Health Limited"), 250 invoices in mixed states, about 109 payments.
  • Perturbations (--perturb): a blocking "What's new" modal, a flaky network (1 to 4 s latency, 8% HTTP 500), and session expiry mid-task.
  • Per episode: success, collateral damage, irreversible changes, false completion, gave up or timed out, steps, tokens, dollars, wall time.

The diff lives in swm/dbdiff.py (about 90 lines, MySQL and Postgres). What counts as a legitimate change for each task is in swm/tasks_*.py.

结果

Clean condition. Full table with perturbations and per-skill breakdown: reports/phase0_results.md.

Model App n Success [95% CI] Clean success Collateral Irreversible False completion
Luna Invoice Ninja 67 87% [76–93] 87% 0% 0% 6%
Luna Dolibarr 72 49% [37–60] 44% 6% 0% 18%
Luna Odoo 17 72 78% [67–86] 68% 15% 6% 6%
Luna Odoo 18 72 76% [65–85] 64% 21% 10% 6%
UI-TARS-7B Invoice Ninja 72 19% [12–30] 18% 14% 3% 26%
UI-TARS-7B Dolibarr 36 8% [3–22] 8% 0% 0% 22%
UI-TARS-7B Odoo 17 36 17% [8–32] 14% 19% 11% 17%
UI-TARS-7B Odoo 18 36 22% [12–38] 19% 31% 8% 22%

Neither agent was trained on any of these apps, so this table measures app difficulty, not transfer.

存储库布局

swm/            harness, agents, database diff, per-app tasks and verifiers, report
  apps/         one adapter per app (login, snapshot, restore, capture)
envs/           docker compose files and credential templates, images pinned by digest
results/        phase0_episodes.jsonl: one line per published episode
reports/        write-up, result tables, failure taxonomy, world-model probe
tests/          unit tests, including one that rebuilds the published table
docs/           adding an agent, adding an app
colab/          serving UI-TARS-1.5-7B with vLLM on a Colab GPU

局限性

  • Small samples, one run per task. Intervals are wide; several differences between cells are inside them.
  • Collateral whitelists are hand-built per app. App-generated noise (sessions, counters, wizards) is whitelisted by inspection and listed in code. A different whitelist would move collateral rates by a few points. The reset-to-draft case does not depend on it.
  • The diff copies every table, which is fine at this data size and would not scale to a large database.
  • A harness bug was found and fixed mid-run. 12 Invoice Ninja episodes could not be rerun and are excluded; counting them as failures is reported alongside.
  • Developed on macOS. The unit tests run on Linux in CI; the full harness has not been run on Linux.
  • Raw step logs and screenshots are not in the repo (about 800 MB). The per-episode summaries are.

The write-up's limitations section is longer and more specific.

相关工作

State-based grading of agents is an active area. Agent-Diff diffs full environment state for API agents on Slack, Linear, Box and Calendar replicas. EntWorld verifies enterprise GUI agents by querying Odoo and EspoCRM databases. WebArena and WorkArena are the standard web-agent benchmarks, and this harness is built on BrowserGym. What this repo adds is the same tasks across two major versions of one app, with collateral and irreversible changes reported separately from success.
